Our team wanted to investigate the growth of Kale and
Radishes as a sustainable food source for astronauts while on
the Moon. After researching the regolith soil and determining
that the best results would require at least a 50/50 regolith to
composting soil composition we established several
independent variables to test in our experimentation.
Purpose
RESEARCH
QUESTION
www.reallygreatsite.com 
02
How does the addition of nutrient rich (PLANT-BASED AMINO ACID: Amino
Acids help to increase chlorophyll concentration in the plant leading to a
higher degree of photosynthesis.) and heat impact the growth of Kale and
Radish planted in a 50 percent regolith and 50 percent nitrogen rich soil
composition.

Background
Radish
Our team wanted to identify a sustainable crop
that could be grown through an unmanned
automation process considering the use of
minimal resources and current lunar conditions.
Kale, or leaf cabbage, belongs to a group of
cabbage cultivars grown for their edible leaves.
Kale plants have green or purple leaves, and
the central leaves do not form a head.
Kale benefits include:
contains fiber, antioxidants, calcium, vitamins C
and K, iron. This is good for the human body. 
Identifying the need for autonomous and
sustainable crops as to reduce the budget,
resources and equipment needs to assist
astronauts in the colonization of the Moon lead us
to develop a self-sustaining grow environment. 
NASA and the Artemis project has identified the
need for efficient and successful food production
given the lunar environment and harsh conditions.
Radishes typically are ready to harvest between
3-5 weeks after planting the seeds.
It takes 22-70 days to start growing.
Radishes are a part of the Brassicaceae family
(Mustard or Cabbage).
This vegetable has a pungent flavor and is
mostly eaten raw
Radishes are rich in antioxidants and minerals
like calcium and potassium. These nutrients can
lower blood pressure and reduce the risk of heart
disease.

HYPOTHESIS

Results
Summary
See attached student lab book. Figure 1
Our growth for all plants that germinated showed a
significant improvement by all that were given the
Nitrogen rich soil. Both height and leaf count were
significantly improved under the independent
variable of nutrient rich soil containing the Nitrogen
and Amino Acide soil additive.
Conclusion
We have concluded that it is possible to design an
autonomous sustainable grow environment on the Moon
given the following conditions. A soil composition of
regolith and nitrogen rich soil along with a grow
environment that can regulate temperature, UV exposure,
CO2 levels, water and protection from extreme lunar
conditions.

The Project Stellars Innovation plan, Is a rover that will be sent to the moon with a self 
contained growing environment. So when astronauts land on the moon they will already have 
a large supply of seedlings, and a potential food supply . The rover will have a large inside 
containing seedlings, adult plants, and a self-watering system, with artificial light. All of the 
plants have a track underneath so when they grow they will be moved into a freezer 
underneath. To keep them from rotting.
Project stellar is also considering a lunar orbiter that would be like a space station, but above 
the moon. This lunar orbiter would grow plants in a contained growing environment powered 
by solar energy. It would grow many types of food, with a watering system. When plants are 
fully grown they would be shuttled down to the colonies on the Moon.
